classification.difficultyReason: Follow supplied proof stages, select SSS or SAS from marked givens, and connect matching angles to parallel-line converses; part (d) reuses the test established in part (c).

content.prompt: This question reviews the proofs of the four tests for a quadrilateral to be a parallelogram.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Prove that: If the opposite angles of a quadrilateral are equal, then the quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with $\angle A=\angle C=\alpha$ and $\angle B=\angle D=\beta$.

spec.description: Unshaded quadrilateral ABCD with opposite angle labels alpha and beta; ordinary source-blue outlines rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: A and C have angle alpha; B and D have angle beta. No parallel or equal-side marks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels and edges are permanent givens.

answer.worked:
The interior angles of quadrilateral $ABCD$ sum to $360^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}2\alpha+2\beta&=360^\circ\\\alpha+\beta&=180^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Hence prove that $AB\parallel DC$ and $AD\parallel BC$.

answer.short: $AB\parallel DC$ and $AD\parallel BC$, since each relevant pair of co-interior angles sums to $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$\angle DAB+\angle ADC=\alpha+\beta=180^\circ$, so $AB\parallel DC$ by the converse of the co-interior angle property.

$\angle DAB+\angle ABC=\alpha+\beta=180^\circ$, so $AD\parallel BC$ by the same converse. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Prove that: If the opposite sides of a quadrilateral are equal, then the quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

Let $RSTU$ be a quadrilateral with $RS=UT$ and $RU=ST$.

spec.description: RSTU with vertical RS and UT, matching double ticks on RS and UT, matching triple ticks on ST and RU, and supplied red dashed diagonal SU. Ordinary outlines and equality marks are black.
spec.mathematics: RS=UT and ST=RU; SU is common to the two triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied diagonal and equality marks remain visible in the question.

answer.worked:
In triangles $RSU$ and $TUS$:

$$\begin{align*}RS&=UT&&\text{(given)}\\RU&=ST&&\text{(given)}\\SU&=US&&\text{(common side)}\end{align*}$$

Therefore $\triangle RSU\equiv\triangle TUS$ by SSS.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Hence prove that $RS\parallel UT$ and $RU\parallel ST$.

answer.short: $RS\parallel UT$ and $RU\parallel ST$, using equal matching angles of congruent triangles and the converse of the alternate angle property.
answer.worked:
$\angle RSU=\angle TUS$ because matching angles of congruent triangles are equal. These are alternate angles on transversal $SU$, so $RS\parallel UT$.

Similarly, $\angle RUS=\angle TSU$, so $RU\parallel ST$. Thus both pairs of opposite sides are parallel and $RSTU$ is a parallelogram.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Prove that: If one pair of opposite sides of a quadrilateral are equal and parallel, then the quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

Let $KLMN$ be a quadrilateral with $KL=NM$ and $KL\parallel NM$.

spec.description: KLMN with vertical KN and LM, descending KL and NM carrying matching double ticks and single parallel arrows, and a supplied red dashed diagonal KM. Ordinary outlines, ticks and parallel marks are black.
spec.mathematics: KL=NM and KL parallel NM; KM is common to the two triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied marks and the auxiliary diagonal remain visible.

answer.worked:
In triangles $KLM$ and $MNK$:

$$\begin{align*}KL&=MN&&\text{(given)}\\\angle LKM&=\angle NMK&&\text{(alternate angles, }KL\parallel NM\text{)}\\KM&=MK&&\text{(common side)}\end{align*}$$

Therefore $\triangle KLM\equiv\triangle MNK$ by SAS.

answer.short: $KN\parallel LM$, since $\angle NKM=\angle LMK$ are equal alternate angles.
answer.worked:
$\angle NKM=\angle LMK$ because matching angles of congruent triangles are equal. These are alternate angles on transversal $KM$, so $KN\parallel LM$.

Together with the given $KL\parallel NM$, this proves that $KLMN$ is a parallelogram.

children.label: d
children.prompt:
Prove that: If the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other, then the quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

Let $EFGH$ be a quadrilateral whose diagonals meet at $O$ and bisect each other.

spec.description: Unshaded EFGH with horizontal EF and HG. Solid diagonals EG and HF intersect at O. EO and OG have double ticks; HO and OF have triple ticks. Ordinary source-blue lines and marks are black.
spec.mathematics: EO=OG and HO=OF; E,O,G and H,O,F are collinear.
spec.answerVisibility: Both diagonals, intersection label and all equality marks are supplied givens.

answer.worked:
In triangles $EHO$ and $GFO$:

$$\begin{align*}EO&=GO&&\text{(given)}\\HO&=FO&&\text{(given)}\\\angle EOH&=\angle GOF&&\text{(vertically opposite angles)}\end{align*}$$

Therefore $\triangle EHO\equiv\triangle GFO$ by SAS.

answer.short: $EH=FG$ by matching sides, and $EH\parallel FG$ by equal alternate angles.
answer.worked:
$EH=FG$ because matching sides of congruent triangles are equal.

$\angle HEO=\angle FGO$ because matching angles of congruent triangles are equal. These are alternate angles on transversal $EG$, so $EH\parallel FG$.

children.label: iii
children.prompt: Explain why this proves that $EFGH$ is a parallelogram.

answer.short: One pair of opposite sides, $EH$ and $FG$, are equal and parallel, so $EFGH$ is a parallelogram.
answer.worked: Part (ii) establishes that the opposite sides $EH$ and $FG$ are equal and parallel. By the test proved in part (c), $EFGH$ is a parallelogram.
